requirements.description: Ask and stream: the owner submits a shopping question and sees ordered research progress until exactly one terminal state.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/chat streams data-progress parts in the order candidates, offers, validate, compare.
Each run ends in exactly one of completed, failed, or cancelled.
The UI shows the current stage, disables input while running, and offers Cancel.

requirements.description: Cited comparison: a completed run shows a comparison of 1-3 candidates whose citation markers resolve to Exa citations from the same run.
acceptanceCriteria: Every rendered source link is a citation URL returned by Exa in this run.
Out-of-range markers are removed and counted; paragraphs with no resolved marker are visibly flagged uncited.
All cases in evals/cases/citations.json and evals/cases/citations-spaced.json produce their expected results, including markers written with spaces such as [2, 5, 6] (CR-001).

(v1.1) Comparison text containing '{' or '}' is cut before the first such character and its citations resolved on the kept text; the UI notes "Exa's answer ended in malformed output, which is not shown."; if no letter remains, the comparison is replaced by that note (D-042, EV-012 comparison cases).

requirements.description: Authentic, relevant merchant offers: only direct, validated merchant product pages for the candidate model are offers; other pages are labeled evidence or rejected; prices are never invented or edited.
acceptanceCriteria: Every displayed offer has merchant host, positive price, supported ISO currency, canonical http(s) URL from this run, availability enum value, source exa, and retrievedAt.
Aggregator, editorial, non-listing, price-less, and merchant-mismatch pages appear only in a separately labeled evidence section.
Irrelevant products, unsupported currencies, URLs not from the run, and non-http URLs never appear as offers.

All 54 cases in evals/cases/offer-classification.json produce their labeled outcome, category, and offer fields, except that L29 and Y03 produce the superseding labels recorded in evals/cases/offer-classification-v1-1.json (D-031, D-032).
(v1.1) Marketplace and search-or-category pages also appear only as labeled evidence (REQ-016).

requirements.description: Currency-safe ranking: offers group by USD, SGD, JPY with the selected market's currency first, sort deterministically within a group, and are never compared across currencies.
acceptanceCriteria: All cases in evals/cases/ranking-currency.json produce the expected groups and order.
A seeded property test over 1,000 generated offer lists shows no mixed-currency group and no lost or duplicated offers beyond the canonical-URL collapse.

requirements.description: Failure recovery: Exa errors and cancellation end the run with a typed, visible reason, partial results are labeled, and live mode never falls back to fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: 401, 402 or credit errors, 429, 5xx, timeout, no candidates, and no offers each yield the specified data-error kind or empty state; a client cancel aborts the Exa call, ends the stream, and shows the client-side cancelled state.
A failure after the candidates stage sets partial true and keeps already validated products visible.
The next question works after any failure.

requirements.description: Spend guard and cache: at most 5 Exa requests per question by construction, at most 3 for a normal question, 6-hour cache, monthly limits, and stop on exhausted credits.
acceptanceCriteria: No sequence of candidates, retries, or errors makes a sixth Exa call in one run.
A repeated question within the TTL makes no Exa call and shows the original retrievedAt.
Monthly request and cost limits block calls before they are made; a 402 or credit error blocks later calls until reset.
Each response's costDollars.total is added to the ledger and shown in the run's usage.
(v1.1) Image fetching never takes a RequestBudget token, never calls Exa, and never writes the Exa ledger.

requirements.description: Local and key safety: the server listens only on 127.0.0.1, rejects foreign Host or Origin, and the Exa key never leaves the server process.
acceptanceCriteria: The listen address is hard-coded to 127.0.0.1; requests with a foreign Host or cross-origin Origin get 403.
A test key string is absent from a production build, server logs, .cache/ (including .cache/images/), evals/fixtures/, API responses, and browser storage.

(v1.1) Every server response except /api/image/:id carries the Content-Security-Policy in docs/futari/ARCHITECTURE.md 'Content-Security-Policy', so the browser loads scripts, styles, images, fonts and API calls only from 127.0.0.1; the Host/Origin guard also covers /api/image/:id.

(v1.2) The browser contacts no third party except the owner-initiated top-level navigation to a server-returned https://checkout.stripe.com/ URL and Stripe's redirect back (D-055); the Content-Security-Policy is unchanged; all commerce routes, including POST /api/stripe/webhook, sit behind the same Host/Origin guard.
(v1.2) STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET follow the same rule as the Exa key: absent from the build, logs, responses, .cache/, .data/, fixtures, and tracked files (REQ-023, EV-021).

requirements.description: Live acceptance (v1.2, replaces the v1.1 8-query suite, D-044): the Stripe sandbox acceptance in evals/cases/live-acceptance-v1-2.json passes within the live limits before v1.2 is declared complete. The v1.1 EV-016 runs stay committed as history.
acceptanceCriteria: Scenarios A1-A8 in evals/cases/live-acceptance-v1-2.json all pass in the last permitted run (at most 2 runs): USD, SGD, and JPY sandbox payments marked paid only by verified webhooks; a declined card and a cancelled checkout end cancelled with the cart unchanged; a resent event is answered duplicate; superseded and cancelled sessions are expired at Stripe; unsigned or wrongly signed deliveries get 400.

Across the run: 0 orders paid without a verified completed or async-succeeded event, 0 live-mode objects, 0 duplicate paid transitions, 0 sessions whose amount or currency differs from the order, 0 charges outside the sandbox.
The owner answers yes to audit items H1-H5, recorded in .futari/evidence/live/ev-023-run-<n>-audit.md.
Exa use stays within 30 requests and $0.40 of reported cost plan-wide from free credits (smoke ≤ 5, EV-023 ≤ 25); Stripe use is sandbox only; the run log contains no key, secret, or card number.

requirements.description: Persistent local history: the conversation survives reloads through versioned, validated localStorage and can be cleared with confirmation; no secret is stored in the browser.
acceptanceCriteria: After a reload the full conversation, including results, is restored.
Clear history asks for confirmation, then empties the thread and removes kensaku.history.v1.
Invalid stored data is discarded with a visible notice.
(v1.1) The frozen MVP history payload evals/fixtures/history/mvp-history-xm5-sg.json, loaded unchanged, renders as v1.1 product cards with the image fallback and without key-spec or reason sections.
(v1.2) History stays at version 1; offers gain an optional id; offers without an id (history saved before v1.2) render with a disabled 'Ask again to buy' button and the rest of the card unchanged.

requirements.description: Frontend quality and components: the UI uses unmodified official AI Elements and shadcn/ui components, has a persistent market selector, and meets accessibility, layout, and owner visual review. (v1.1: in both themes, with the image-first cards.) (v1.2: including the simulated cart, dialogs, and checkout return states.)

axe reports zero serious or critical violations on empty, running, completed, and error states; the journey works by keyboard alone. (v1.1) This holds in the dark and the light theme.
At 375 px width there is no horizontal page scroll.
The owner records visual review of the v1.1 cards on desktop and mobile widths in both themes in .futari/evidence/JM-105.md.
(v1.1) No new design system or hand-edited component is introduced, and the CSS variables in src/web/index.css are unchanged.

(v1.2) The cart sheet, currency-replace dialog, and every checkout return panel have zero serious or critical axe violations in both themes and work by keyboard alone; the only new component is the official shadcn sheet installed unmodified with the pinned CLI and recorded in components.lock.json.
(v1.2) The owner records visual review of the commerce UI on desktop and mobile widths in both themes in .futari/evidence/JM-204.md.

requirements.description: Theme: dark is the default for first-time visitors, an accessible toggle in the header switches between dark and light, the choice persists, and the first paint already uses the right theme.
acceptanceCriteria: With no stored preference, the page renders dark regardless of the operating system's prefers-color-scheme.

A header button with an accessible name ('Switch to light theme' or 'Switch to dark theme') toggles the theme by mouse and keyboard and stores 'dark' or 'light' in localStorage kensaku.theme.v1; reloads keep the choice.

The theme class and color-scheme are set by a blocking script before the app bundle runs, so with the bundle delayed the page already shows the chosen theme; an invalid stored value or unavailable localStorage falls back to dark without an error.
Theming uses the shadcn/ui class-based .dark convention and the existing CSS variables in src/web/index.css only.

requirements.description: Image-first product cards: each recommended product gets its own generously sized card with a large image, name, price summary, key specifications, recommendation reason, and merchant offers, with research details available but collapsed.
acceptanceCriteria: At 1280 px viewport width product cards sit two per row, each at least 480 px wide; at 375 px they sit one per row with no horizontal page scroll.

Each card's image is full-bleed: it spans the card's full width (no inner padding) at a 4:3 aspect ratio above the text; at 1280 px it is at least 360 px tall, and at 375 px it is at least 300 px wide (so at least 225 px tall).

A card shows, in order: product name (candidate brand and name), image with caption, price summary ('From <lowest listed price> <code>') from offers in the market's currency only, up to 5 key specifications, the cited recommendation reason, the merchant offer list, an 'Other markets' disclosure when other-currency offers exist, and a 'Research details' disclosure with evidence and rejected counts; the card reads key specs and the reason only from the normalized data-products entry fields, never from the raw candidate.

The product heading names the product, never a merchant; each offer row names its merchant host, merchant name, price with ISO currency code, availability, retrieval time, and a 'View offer' link, so a product with several merchants reads as one product with several offers.

Reason citations render with the AI Elements inline-citation component and resolve under the EV-004 rule after the leaked-structure cut (D-042); the comparison text and its Sources stay above the cards.

requirements.description: Real product images: images come only from the product pages of this run's merchant offers or from the manufacturer's page, under rules I1-I3, with loading states, attribution, and a graceful fallback; nothing is generated or invented.
acceptanceCriteria: The pipeline selects up to 4 image candidates per product with rules I1 and I2 in evals/cases/image-selection.json, and the proxy accepts bytes only under rule I3; no image ever comes from aggregator, editorial, marketplace, search-or-category, merchant-mismatch, or rejected pages.
The card shows a skeleton while an image loads, tries candidates in order, and shows a 'No verified product image' fallback (no broken-image icon) when none loads.
The caption names the source page's host and its product title as Exa reported it (so a colour variant is named), and the image's alt text is '<brand> <name>, image from <host>'.
No image is generated, edited, or taken from a source outside this run's Exa results.

requirements.description: Image proxy safety and cache: the server fetches and serves only image URLs registered by a research run, blocks private networks, validates bytes, and caches bytes and metadata on disk.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/image/:id serves only ids registered by a run (SHA-256 of the image URL); unknown or malformed ids get 404 without any outbound request; requests whose Sec-Fetch-Site header is present and not same-origin get 403, and every response carries Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin.

Only http and https URLs on ports 80 or 443 are fetched; every connection, including each of at most 3 redirects, goes to an address that was resolved once for that hop and checked: IPv4 must be public unicast and IPv6 must be in 2000::/3 outside 2001::/32, 2001:db8::/32 and 2002::/16; URL hosts that are IP literals are checked the same way. The connection is made with node:http or node:https to the checked address.

Fetches send no cookies, credentials, or Referer, time out after 8 s, stop at 5 MiB, and accept only bytes passing rule I3; responses use the sniffed image type, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'.

Accepted bytes are reused for 7 days and then refetched while the registry entry exists; registry entries are pruned 30 days after their last registration, and bytes are evicted oldest-first above 500 MB in total; rule I3 rejections are cached for 24 hours and upstream failures for 10 minutes; image fetching never uses Exa or the Exa budget.

requirements.description: Market relevance and currency presentation: offer searches name the market, the card's main offer list shows only the selected market's currency, and other currencies are collapsed under 'Other markets'.
acceptanceCriteria: The offer search query is '<brand> <name> price <United States|Singapore|Japan> buy' with userLocation set to the market.

A card's main offer list and price summary use only offers in the market's currency; offers in other supported currencies appear in a collapsed 'Other markets (may not ship to <market name>)' disclosure, and no conversion is ever shown.
When a product has no offer in the market's currency, the main list says 'No <market name> offers found' and the Other markets disclosure stays collapsed.
Prices show the amount with the ISO currency code (for example '289.00 SGD'); symbols such as '$' are never shown alone.

requirements.description: Non-merchant pages and currency symbols (CR-002 and v1.1 additions): search, category, editorial, and second-hand marketplace pages never appear as merchant offers, and unambiguous currency symbols are recognized.
acceptanceCriteria: Classification applies the rule additions 4, 5, 5a, 5b, 5c and 7 recorded in evals/cases/offer-classification-v1-1.json ruleAdditions and docs/futari/ARCHITECTURE.md.
EV-011 passes all 79 cases in evals/cases/offer-classification-v1-1.json, including the run 1 Rakuten search page (Q5-O1, case N33).
EV-001 applies the L29 and Y03 supersessions and passes the remaining MVP cases with their original labels.

requirements.description: Registered offers and cart rules (D-046, D-048, D-054): only offers registered on the server by a research run can be added to the single, server-owned, one-currency cart, under the rules in evals/cases/commerce-rules.json.
acceptanceCriteria: Every validated merchant offer in a run gets the deterministic offerId of evals/cases/commerce-rules.json rules.offerId, is registered in .cache/offers/<id>.json, and carries id in data-products.
POST /api/cart/items accepts only { offerId, quantity?, replace? } (strict); price, currency, and product data always come from the registry; unknown offerIds are refused.

Cart operations reproduce every outcome, error code, precedence, and resulting cart in evals/cases/commerce-rules.json (one currency, replace, quantity 1-10, 20 lines, Stripe minimums, total cap, out-of-stock refusal).
HTTP statuses follow docs/futari/ARCHITECTURE.md 'HTTP API' (v1.2); the cart persists across server restarts in .data/commerce/state.json.

requirements.description: Demo checkout price distinct from the last-observed price (D-045): the demo unit price is the observed price copied at add time, never refreshed, and always labeled separately.
acceptanceCriteria: Each cart line stores demoUnitAmountMinor (the minor-unit form of the registered price, rules.minorUnits) and observed { amount, currency, retrievedAt, merchantHost } exactly as evals/cases/commerce-rules.json snapshotCases require.
Every cart line shows 'Demo checkout price <amount> <code>' and, in a separate element, 'Last observed <amount> <code> on <host>, <local date and time>'; totals are labeled 'Demo total'.
Each Stripe line item's description states that the demo price was copied from the price last observed on the merchant host at the stored time (EV-019).

requirements.description: Stripe-hosted Checkout through the official Stripe Node SDK (D-052): stripe@23.1.0, apiVersion 2026-10-28.endive, the exact session request in evals/cases/checkout-session-request.json, no currency conversion.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json pins stripe 23.1.0 exactly; src/commerce/stripe-port.ts is the only module that imports stripe and constructs it with apiVersion '2026-10-28.endive'.
buildCheckoutSessionRequest output deep-equals every case in evals/cases/checkout-session-request.json, and StripeCheckoutPort passes exactly those params and options to checkout.sessions.create.

The server returns the session url only if it starts with https://checkout.stripe.com/ and the session has livemode false; the client checks the prefix again and navigates with window.location.assign.
USD, SGD, and JPY sessions are created with the order's own currency and minor-unit amounts; no exchange rate or conversion exists anywhere (adaptive_pricing disabled).

requirements.description: Verified webhooks and order state (D-047, D-057): orders change only through signature-verified Stripe events, the cancel route, and the supersede step, exactly as in evals/cases/webhook-events.json.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/stripe/webhook verifies the Stripe-Signature over the raw body with stripe.webhooks.constructEvent and a 300 s tolerance; invalid, stale, missing, or tampered signatures get 400 and change nothing.
Live-mode events or objects get 400; processed event ids are stored and a repeat gets 200 duplicate; unknown orders and session, amount, or currency mismatches get 200 and change nothing.
State transitions, cart clearing, declinedAttempts, anomalies, and the cancel and checkout route behaviour match every case in evals/cases/webhook-events.json.
Only a verified checkout.session.completed with payment_status paid or a checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded sets an order paid.

requirements.description: Payment scenarios: successful, declined, cancelled, expired or superseded, and duplicate-webhook scenarios each end in their defined state, deterministically in CI and live in the sandbox.
acceptanceCriteria: In CI, the fake hosted page drives success, decline then back, back without paying, and a duplicate delivery to the states and messages in docs/futari/EVALUATION_PLAN.md 'Commerce UI (EV-022)' checks 5-8.
In the sandbox, EV-023 scenarios A1-A8 pass.

requirements.description: Simulated labeling: every purchase is labeled as simulated, and nothing implies that a real merchant order was placed.
acceptanceCriteria: The label strings in docs/futari/ARCHITECTURE.md 'Labels' (v1.2) appear on the cart, each line, the totals, the checkout button, the paid panel, and the order badges.
Stripe line item names start with 'Simulated: ' and descriptions say no order is placed with the merchant and no real payment is taken (EV-019).
None of 'Order confirmed', 'Order placed', 'Thank you for your order', 'Purchase complete', 'has shipped' appears in the UI (case-insensitive, EV-022 check 11); the owner audit H1-H5 passes (EV-023).

requirements.description: Sandbox-only Stripe keys and secret handling (D-050): live keys and real payments are impossible, and credentials stay server-side and out of Git.
acceptanceCriteria: The server refuses to start when STRIPE_SECRET_KEY contains _live_ or does not start with sk_test_, rk_test_, or rkcs_test_, or when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET lacks the whsec_ prefix; the error names the variable but never prints the value.
Checkout is enabled only when both values are present; GET /api/cart reports checkoutConfigured; GET /api/health is unchanged from v1.1 and says nothing about Stripe.
Any Stripe session with livemode true is refused (502, order failed, no url) and any event or object with livemode true gets 400.

No key or secret pattern ((sk|rk|rkcs|pk)_(test|live)_[A-Za-z0-9]{8,} or whsec_[A-Za-z0-9]{8,}) appears in tracked files, dist/, logs, API responses, .cache/, or .data/ (EV-021); .env.local and .data/ are gitignored.

requirements.description: Commerce UI: add-to-cart controls, the currency-replace dialog, the cart sheet, checkout return states, and the order list, built from unmodified official shadcn/ui components.
acceptanceCriteria: Offer items in the main list and Other markets have 'Add to cart' with an aria-label naming product and host; disabled states and tooltips for offers without id ('Ask again to buy'), out-of-stock ('Out of stock'), invalid price ('Price can't be charged'), and below-minimum ('Below Stripe's minimum').
The header cart button shows the line count; the cart sheet shows the banner, lines with quantity controls, remove, clear, demo total, checkout, and the 10 newest orders with status badges.

The success, waiting, cancelled, unknown-checkout, checkout-failed, not-configured, and 'Checkout link expired' states show the texts in docs/futari/PRODUCT_SPEC.md '(v1.2) Simulated commerce journey'; the declined note is best-effort and appears only when Stripe reported a decline (R-30).
EV-022 checks 1-15 pass.

tasks.title: Stripe adapter: pinned SDK, CheckoutPort, session request, webhook verification, sandbox-only config
acceptanceCriteria: package.json adds stripe at exactly 23.1.0 (pnpm-lock.yaml updated); no other dependency changes.

src/commerce/port.ts defines CheckoutPort, SessionResult, the typed errors, and its own CheckoutOrderInput (structural; it does not import JM-201 code); src/commerce/session-request.ts implements buildCheckoutSessionRequest; EV-019 passes.

src/commerce/stripe-port.ts is the only stripe importer: StripeCheckoutPort (apiVersion '2026-10-28.endive', timeout 10000 ms, maxNetworkRetries 0; any expire error surfaces as one typed stripe-error, because the shape for a non-open session is unknown until the JM-203 smoke; refuses livemode sessions and urls outside https://checkout.stripe.com/) and verifyWebhook(rawBody, header, secret) using stripe.webhooks.constructEvent with tolerance 300; src/commerce/fake-port.ts implements FakeCheckoutPort with recorded calls and the scripted outcomes the EV-020 route cases use: expire ok | ok-delayed | error; retrieve open | complete | expired | error; create ok | error | livemode | url:<value>.

src/server/config.ts parses STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET per D-050 into an optional ServerConfig.stripe { secretKey, webhookSecret } (present only when both are set); AppConfig is unchanged, so existing test helpers that build AppConfig literals still typecheck; .env.example documents both empty; EV-021 checks 1, 2, and 4 pass (checks 3 and 5 are completed by JM-203 in the same test file).

src/commerce/stripe-port.ts also exports signTestPayload(payload, secret, timestamp) wrapping stripe.webhooks.generateTestHeaderString, for tests and the test-only fake hosted page, so stripe stays imported in one module; the Stripe-facing label strings ('Simulated: ' prefix, descriptions) live in src/commerce/session-request.ts and are frozen by EV-019.
Never contact live Stripe; tests use FakeCheckoutPort or a stubbed SDK client and secrets built at runtime.

src/commerce/fake-hosted.ts serves the test-only page (Pay, Decline, Back) and the test-only routes POST /__test/commerce/reset, /__test/commerce/checkout-configured { value }, /__test/commerce/withhold-webhooks { value }, and /__test/commerce/expire-open-order (sets the open order's expiresAt in the past) only when NODE_ENV=test and fixture mode (EV-022 isolation and checks 9-10); tests/e2e/commerce-slice.spec.ts runs research → add → checkout → fake page → signed webhook → paid with zero non-local requests.

Sandbox smoke (docs/futari/EVALUATION_PLAN.md 'Slice smoke (JM-203, v1.2)') with the owner's sandbox key and Stripe CLI: USD, SGD, and JPY sessions created, retrieved, and expired; one owner-paid USD purchase marked paid only after the verified webhook; one owner decline with 4000 0000 0000 0002 then back (whether payment_intent.payment_failed arrives is recorded); one expire of an already-expired session with the real error shape recorded; one stripe events resend answered duplicate; ≤ 5 Exa requests; log committed under .futari/evidence/live/.
